standard_prerequisites: Same chapter: definition-trace-pairing (the symmetric bilinear form Q_{L/K}(alpha, beta) = Trace_{L/K}(alpha beta), source lines 2730-2738), lemma-trace-and-norm-tower (traces compose in towers), lemma-trace-and-norm-from-minimal-polynomial (trace of a power from the minimal polynomial), lemma-separable-first and lemma-finite-purely-inseparable (the purely inseparable degree p layer), lemma-characteristic-vs-minimal-polynomial (minimal = characteristic polynomial for the multiplication map), lemma-recognize-separable (separable iff distinct roots), lemma-sums-of-powers (power sums detect nonvanishing)
core_obligations: (2) iff (3): if Trace(gamma) != 0 then Q(alpha, gamma/alpha) = Trace(gamma) != 0 for every nonzero alpha, so Q is nondegenerate; the converse is immediate

Purely inseparable degree p case: for L = K(alpha) with alpha^p in K, char p, the minimal polynomial of alpha^i is x^p - alpha^{pi}, so Trace(alpha^i) = 0 for i = 1, ..., p-1 and Trace(1) = p = 0; the trace is identically zero
Inseparable implies (2) fails: the purely inseparable degree p layer L/K' (lemmas separable-first, finite-purely-inseparable) has identically zero trace, and the tower lemma kills the full trace

Separable implies (2): by induction on the degree, reduce via the tower lemma to L = K(alpha) (the parenthetical 'use that if the trace is nonzero then it is surjective' is the author's own terse carried step for the induction), read the minimal polynomial P as characteristic polynomial, get d distinct roots alpha_1, ..., alpha_d as eigenvalues, and conclude by the power sums lemma that some Trace(alpha^e) = sum alpha_i^e is nonzero
proof_roadmap: Compute the purely inseparable degree p case and lift it to the inseparable direction
Run the separable direction by induction, eigenvalues and power sums
